== Biography ==

William’s birth date and birthplace, and his place of death, remain unknown. The older local 1516 estimate and High Street death location are unsupported; the records describe property, not those vital events.

'''Current father assessment, 16 October 2026:''' [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]] is the property-defined Saltmarket John’s '''probable son''', inferred from the combined title sequence. This is below documented parentage; Eufame Craig’s maternity and the imported profile’s identity remain unresolved. [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/branches/early-scottish-records/#saltmarket-probable-father Evidence and alternatives].

== Selected Glasgow–Stirling working identity — 15 October 2026 ==

The local family tree now models '''John de Glasgu, burgess of Glasgow in 1447–1455''', and '''John Glasgw/Glesgw of Stirling in 1475–1479/80''' as '''one uncertain working identity'''. The separate record-group accounts and their original citations remain intact.

Select the Glasgow burgess of 1447–1455 and the Stirling witness of 1475–1479/80 as the same man, at low confidence. Both groups use compatible John de Glasgu/Glasgw name forms in burgh-property witnessing, and the August 1475 catalogue places the Stirling John among burgesses. An adult active in 1447 could still witness in 1480 in his fifties or older. The conventional circa-1450 Stirling birth was inferred from an assumed young adult in 1475; it cannot establish a second man. A single compatible civic career is the simpler working model than inserting another generation from that estimate.

'''Limits and alternatives:''' No shared holding, relative, trade, personal seal or distinctive repeated associate joins the cities. The Glasgow-to-Stirling change is not itself evidence of migration. Father–son, other kin and two unrelated namesakes remain viable alternatives. The name may still be a personal byname; this selection does not prove hereditary surname transmission. The two Glasgow acts remain one high-confidence group and the three Stirling acts another; only their cross-group identity is selected uncertain. No birth, death or additional parent is inferred.

The selected uncertain father links to Saltmarket candidate Glasgow-1095 and Alan Glasgow-3023 remain unchanged. Glasgow-1095 is still only a provisional Saltmarket representative: if it instead represents the older witness, that father link collapses as a duplicate identity. The earlier Malcolm father candidate remains unselected. Identity and father–son alternatives between the Glasgow and Stirling groups are not combined.

This changes the working ancestor’s earliest record from 1475 to 1447. It does not add a father edge, merge a WikiTree profile, upgrade any relationship, or improve the fixed profile-connectivity score. Five previously known occurrences are assigned conditionally to one working person; this is not five newly found records. [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/branches/early-scottish-records/#glasgow-stirling-identity Full comparison and current model].

Sources: ''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine'' (1846), acts of 21 June 1447 and April 1455 (Blackhouse BL68/GUA12418 and BL82/GUA12430; April day disputed); ''Charters and Other Documents Relating to the Royal Burgh of Stirling'' (1884), abstracts of 11 April 1475 and 2 March 1479/80; NRS B66/25/43, 8 August 1475. No new original inspection is claimed.

| '''Possible father:''' [[Space:John_Glasgw_of_Stirling|John Glasgw of Stirling (fl. 1475–1479/80)]]. His adult activity in 1475–1480 places him in the right generation to be the father of John, estimated born about 1480, and the uncommon surname and civic-property setting support the possibility.

'''John Glasgow''' was probably born about '''1480''' and died before '''21 October 1553'''. This is a conditional birth estimate based on the possible identification with the adult John alias Smith in 1506, not an independently recorded age. The Saltmarket property-holder is securely located in 1527; no birth or baptism record is known.

He lived in Glasgow and held property in the burgh. A possible earlier identification is '''John of Glasgow alias Smith''', joint acquirer with Sir Allan Smith of a High Street annual rent in 1506. In 1527 '''John Glasgow''' held the identifiable Saltmarket tenement between John Rankin and James Young that later passed to [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]]. The shared name, city and property milieu keep that identification plausible. The two records concern different holdings, and no later deed repeats the Smith alias or recites the 1506 title, so activity in 1506 cannot be treated as a proved fact about the Saltmarket owner.

'''Eufame Craig''' was probably John's wife. In 1564 she still held a widow's liferent in the rear of the same property block. That reserved interest fits naturally if it was created while John held the property and then survived the transfer of the fee to William. [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]] is now assessed as John's '''probable son''', below documented parentage. Eufame's maternity is not established; she could have been a stepmother. The title evidence is that William held John's exact burdened title by 20 February 1528/29, only about twenty-one and a half months after John's recorded possession.

John was dead by 21 October 1553, when Rankin's adjoining property was bounded by the lands of the late John Glasgow. He was not [[Glasgow-1093|John Glasgow]], husband of [[Spreull-4|Jonet Spreull]], who remained alive in 1565, nor the much earlier burgess recorded in 1447 and 1455.

=== High Street property, 1506 ===

On 28 April 1506 Agnes, daughter and heir of Robert Watson, sold a ground-annual of 4s from a tenement on Glasgow High Street to Sir Allan Smith and '''John of Glasgow alias Smith'''. Sir Allan's property was the northern boundary.<ref name="AliasSmith">Glasgow University Archives, Blackhouse Charters, GUA BL/204, formerly GUA 16403, instrument dated 28 April 1506; [https://yourscottisharchives.com/catalogues/565b7ef3-fc87-3f6f-aaac-149925faa39d?component-id=7cdbf375-dc6d-3de3-b53a-86376e2106da Your Scottish Archives catalogue description]. The complete instrument has not been inspected.</ref>

The expression ''alias Smith'' may indicate:

* an occupational surname;
* a paternal or maternal surname used for identification;
* a household or family association;
* or a second established name.

The instrument does not call John a smith or armourer and does not state that Sir Allan Smith was his father, brother or other relative.

The catalogue's legacy description contains the malformed form ''Watsonm'', which must be checked against the instrument. The complete instrument has not yet been transcribed. Its witnesses, terms of joint acquisition, survivorship, source of title and precise alias syntax may materially affect the identification.

=== Saltmarket property, 1527–1553 ===

==== 2 May 1527 ====

Andrew Loppe resigned in favour of Master James Houston, subdean of Glasgow, an annual rent of 4s payable from the tenement of '''John Glasgow'''.<ref name="JohnSaltmarket1527">''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine'', act dated 2 May 1527, recording a four-shilling annual rent from the tenement of John Glasgow; [https://archive.org/details/libercollegiino00annegoog Internet Archive].</ref>

The tenement:

* stood on the west side of the street leading from Glasgow's Market Cross to the South Port;
* lay between John Rankyn's land on the south and the former land of James Young on the north;
* and owed an annual rent of 4s.

The street was the Walkergate or Fullers' Street, now '''Saltmarket'''. John was not resigning the rent; Andrew Loppe held the right to receive it, while John's tenement was burdened by the payment.

A related description places John Rankyn's adjoining tenement between John Glasgow on the north and Andrew Craig on the south. The frontage therefore ran approximately:

# former land of James Young;
# John Glasgow's tenement;
# John Rankyn's tenement;
# Andrew Craig's land.

==== 5 January 1548 ====

The collegiate church's fresh foundation sasine again recorded the same four-shilling annual rent from the tenement of '''John Glasgu''', with the same street position and adjoining holdings: John Rankyn to the south and the former land of James Young to the north.<ref name="JohnSaltmarket1548">''Liber Collegii Nostre Domine'', property inventory dated 5 January 1548, repeating the four-shilling annual rent, location and neighbours of John Glasgu's tenement; [https://archive.org/details/libercollegiino00annegoog Internet Archive].</ref>

The 1527 and 1548 entries concern the same identifiable holding. Because the 1548 act renews sasine in the collegiate foundation's whole property portfolio, its description may copy the 1527 title wording; it does not by itself prove that John remained alive or in possession in 1548.

==== William Glasgow on the same parcel, 1534/35–1535/36 ====

On 17 February 1534/35, John Rankin's adjoining property was bounded by the lands of '''William Glasgow''' on the north and Andrew Craig on the south.<ref name="WilliamBoundary1535">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. IV, protocol 1201, 17 February 1534/35, pp. 73–74.</ref> On 16 March 1535/36 James Young's place was bounded by the lands of the '''late William Glasgow''' on the south and Robert Cochran on the north.<ref name="WilliamDead1536">Ibid., protocol 1233, 16 March 1535/36, pp. 86–87, fol. 87.</ref>

The two lateral boundaries place William on John's exact 1527 parcel. In 1564 William's son John entered a fore tenement as heir of William, his father, still between the late John Rankin south and Robert Young north.<ref name="JohnHeir1564">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. III, protocol 805, 28 October 1564, p. 57.</ref> This is strong property succession evidence, but no inspected act states that the older John was William's father or explains the John-to-William transmission.

==== Dead by 21 October 1553 ====

On 21 October 1553 John Rankyn transferred his adjoining property. It was bounded on the north by the lands of '''q. John Glasgow''', where ''q.'' represents ''quondam'', meaning the late or deceased John Glasgow.<ref name="JohnDead1553">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', act dated 21 October 1553, describing John Rankyn's property as bounded by the lands of the late John Glasgow.</ref>

The property-holder was therefore:

* still used as the parcel's title-name on 5 January 1548, possibly from copied foundation wording;
* expressly deceased by 21 October 1553;
* and associated with one continuously identifiable Saltmarket tenement for at least twenty-one years.

=== Possible Bridgegate appearance, 1536 ===

Protocol 1258 records the transfer of a tenement extending from the South Barras gate towards the bridge over the Clyde. '''John Glasgw''' appears as a witness with Richard Allane, Alexander Myllar, John Waulderston and Adam Lyon.<ref name="John1536">Protocol 1258, 11 July 1536; [https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/William_Hegait_s_protocols_1547_76/WB8NAAAAYAAJ?pg=PA96 published protocol text].</ref>

The chronology makes him a plausible occurrence of the Saltmarket owner. The record does not repeat the property, alias, occupation or relationship, so the identity remains unproved.

=== Family and succession ===

This John is the strongest candidate for [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]]'s father. [[Space:John_Glasgw_of_Stirling|John Glasgw of Stirling]] is the leading candidate for the preceding generation and a plausible father of this John.

That structure is compatible with:

* the Stirling John's adult activity in 1475–1479/80;
* Alias Smith's adult property acquisition in 1506;
* William's activity in the early sixteenth century;
* their shared surname and urban property setting;
* and William naming his proved son John.

It remains an inference. No inspected record calls this John William's brother, father, heir or nearest in blood, and no record identifies the father of William Glasgow.

On 31 December 1534 William Glasgow and Esbell Brade transferred property to their son John Glasgow and his wife Jonet Spreull.<ref name="WilliamBradeSpreull1534">''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', protocol dated 31 December 1534, recording William Glasgow and Esbell Brade, their son John Glasgow and his wife Jonet Spreull.</ref> This proves William's son John, not William's own father or siblings.

=== Distinction from other John Glasgows ===

The Saltmarket owner cannot be [[Glasgow-1093|John Glasgow]], husband of Jonet Spreull. The Saltmarket owner was dead by October 1553, while the younger John remained alive on 24 August 1565 when he transferred a burgage tenement to his son William and reserved liferent to himself and Jonet.<ref name="JohnWilliam1565">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. III, protocol no. 847, p. 73, 24 August 1565.</ref>

He also cannot reasonably be John de Glasgu I, first recorded as a burgess in 1447. Extending that man to 1548 would require an implausibly long adult career.

=== Evidence assessment ===

The secure evidence establishes that:

* John alias Smith jointly acquired a Glasgow High Street annual rent in 1506;
* a John Glasgow held an identifiable Saltmarket tenement in 1527 and his name remained in its 1548 foundation title-description;
* William Glasgow occupied the exact Rankin–Young parcel in 1534/35 and was deceased by 16 March 1535/36;
* William's son John inherited the same fore tenement in 1564;
* that owner was dead by 21 October 1553;
* and he was distinct from John, husband of Jonet Spreull.

The evidence does not prove that Alias Smith and the Saltmarket owner were one man, that the 1536 witness was the same owner, or that he was son of the Stirling John or brother of William Glasgow.

=== Timeline summary ===

* '''before c.1485''' — working birth estimate based on adult participation in the 1506 acquisition
* '''28 April 1506''' — John of Glasgow alias Smith jointly acquires a High Street ground-annual
* '''2 May 1527''' — John Glasgow's west-side Saltmarket tenement owes an annual rent of 4s
* '''11 July 1536''' — John Glasgw witnesses a Bridgegate transaction; possible occurrence
* '''17 February 1534/35''' — Rankin's adjoining property has William Glasgow north
* '''16 March 1535/36''' — James Young's adjoining property has the late William Glasgow south
* '''5 January 1548''' — the same rent, tenement and neighbours are repeated under John Glasgu's name in the foundation sasine
* '''before 21 October 1553''' — John is deceased; adjoining property is bounded by his former lands

'''Secure Alias Smith record:''' 1.

'''Secure Saltmarket property records:''' 3, comprising the 1527 holding, its 1548 continuation and the 1553 deceased-owner boundary.

== For further research ==

* Transcribe GUA BL/204 in full.
* Compare the 1506 witnesses, source of title and property with the Saltmarket holding.
* Trace the Saltmarket tenement after John's death, searching for an heir, widow, assignee or nearest relative.
* Search for ''heres quondam Johannis Glasgu'', ''filius'', ''frater'', ''relicta'', ''proximior de sanguine'' and similar clauses.
* Inspect the full 1536 protocol and neighbouring entries.
* Test the proposed relationship to William Glasgow through property succession rather than naming alone.
* Keep the Alias Smith–Saltmarket identity labelled unproved until a repeated alias, matching property or relationship clause appears.

== Selected working family — 15 October 2026 ==

The local family tree now selects '''John Glasgw of Stirling''' as an '''uncertain''' father of two compatible later bearers. This is an explicit working pedigree, not a newly found parent record.

* '''Saltmarket John''', provisionally represented by [[Glasgow-1095]], is the stronger existing father hypothesis: adult Stirling activity by 1475, compatible consecutive generations and burgh-property networks. The Brady/Brade association is a weak supporting clue. The imported profile mixes identities and may instead represent Stirling John; that alternative collapses this father link.
* '''[[Glasgow-3023|Alan Glasgw]]''' is selected more tentatively as a son from the existing son/brother/nephew comparison. His age and home are unknown. Jedburgh is the court venue, not his residence. Brother, nephew or another early family remain viable.

No mother or unnamed intermediary is invented. Earlier in this review both Glasgow–Stirling models were unselected. The later working-identity section now selects one uncertain identity; a father–son relationship remains an unselected alternative. These models are not combined. Alan’s printed 1494/95 and regnal-year discrepancy still needs JC1/1 collation.

Sources remain the separately cited Stirling abstracts of 11 April 1475 and 2 March 1479/80, NRS B66/25/43 (8 August 1475), the Saltmarket title reconstruction of 1527–1553, and Pitcairn, ''Criminal Trials'' I, part I, p.19. No new original inspection is claimed. [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/branches/early-scottish-records/#stirling-working-family Reasons, alternatives and the selected local tree].


=== Saltmarket John is William’s probable father —16 October2026 ===

The older John Glasgow who held the Saltmarket Rankin–Young tenement in 1527 is assessed as the probable father of William [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow of Saltmarket]]. William occupies the matching parcel by 20 February 1528/29; the later St Andrew prebend rental retains its four-shilling burden, west-side street position and Rankin boundary. The 1534 family settlement and 1564 service as heir then directly identify the younger John [[Glasgow-1093|Glasgow-1093]] as William’s son. Read together, these describe a sustained family title rather than merely two men sharing a surname. Lineal succession from the earlier John to William is the preferred reconstruction, while the last William-to-John step is independently documented. The grade is now probable, below documented or strongly supported. This brings the formal local father assessment into line with the stronger property argument already developed in the research.

The missing 1527–1529 conveyance has not been found. No inspected instrument calls William the earlier John’s son, and no recorded ages distinguish father from brother. A brother, collateral heir or purchase from a namesake remains possible. Indeed, the neighbouring Henryson parcel in the 1528/29 instrument passes between brothers; title succession alone cannot specify kinship. The combined parcel descriptions are correlated, and the later rental is not an independent record of the original transfer. [[Glasgow-1095|John Glasgow, provisional Saltmarket account]] remains a provisional representation of the Saltmarket owner: its identification with the Stirling witness or the 1506 alias-Smith purchaser is not proved. The probable grade applies to the property-defined Saltmarket father hypothesis, not to every imported biographical claim. No mother is inferred: Eufame Craig may have been the earlier John’s widow, but this does not establish her as William’s mother. No Stirling parent, birth estimate, death location or identity merge is upgraded. The live WikiTree father flag remains uncertain; probable is a local research grade.

This is a re-evaluation of an existing father attachment, not a new parent or a newly discovered record. The earlier generic uncertain assessment and its 28 September basis are retained in the structured history. All working family membership and confidently marked paternal connectivity remain unchanged. The printed 1528/29 boundary on p.90 and four-shilling rental on p.36 were freshly inspected; the other title steps retain their earlier maintained source reviews. The original manuscript transfer remains uninspected. Review priorities now rank every non-confident paternal link, including older tree attachments, rather than only the 57 selected working hypotheses.
